evals.prompt: Copy my blog post to Medium by pasting it into a new story. That's all.
evals.expected_output: Should say a pasted story needs 'This story was originally published elsewhere' set (or use Import a story, which adds the canonical), and add an 'Originally published' line linking the original. Should check the copy's page source for the canonical after publishing.
expectations: Sets Medium's canonical via import or the 'originally published' setting
Adds an 'Originally published' line linking the original
Checks the canonical in the copy's source
Makes links absolute and pointing at originals

evals.prompt: A partner site wants to republish my full article but won't add noindex.
evals.expected_output: Should follow the decision order: Google recommends the partner block indexing; if they won't, ask for a canonical link to the original (Bing's guidance); if neither, offer an excerpt with a clear link back, and accept the copy may outrank the original. Should agree terms in writing.
expectations: Asks for noindex first, per Google
Falls back to a canonical link, per Bing
Offers an excerpt with a link if neither
Puts the syndication terms in writing

evals.prompt: I just published this tutorial an hour ago. Cross-post it to dev.to, Hashnode and LinkedIn right now.
evals.expected_output: Should advise waiting until the original is indexed (practice), then set dev.to's canonical_url and Hashnode's republishing URL, and on LinkedIn (no canonical field) add a link back or post a summary. Should record each copy in the publication's list of copies.
expectations: Advises waiting for the original to be indexed first
Sets dev.to canonical_url and Hashnode's original URL
Uses a link back or summary on LinkedIn
Records the copies in the publication's list

evals.prompt: Cross-post my newsletter essay to Substack following my publication's rules.
evals.expected_output: Should read the publication's writing-guide.md and profile.md (CLAUDE.md path → publications/ → ask) for which platforms it uses and how the 'originally published' line reads, and check rights if the essay was commissioned. Substack has no canonical field, so add a link back or post a summary.
expectations: Notes Substack has no canonical field and links back
Checks rights if the piece was written for someone else
